limitations: Mass-spectrometry Intensity values are recorded for only 4 of the top 20 colon transcription factors, while 16 entries are blank (missing observations). A blank record in HPA proteomics denotes an unmeasured protein or a level below the assay detection threshold, not a zero or confirmed biological absence.

Because 16 of 20 proteins lack mass-spectrometry measurements, a true median protein abundance across all twenty genes cannot be calculated without arbitrarily imputing missing values as zero, which would conflate missingness with true biological absence.

Biological absence in colon tissue cannot be inferred from blank MS intensity entries or missing IHC annotations, as MS detection sensitivity depends on dynamic range, peptide detectability, and protein physicochemical properties.

issues: claims[3]: "Only 4 of the 20 genes (YBX1, EGR1, JUND, and ELF3) have Enhanced or Supported IHC records in normal colon tissue across 19 cell-type entries; the remaining 16…" states 16, not among the cells it is bound to (a21 rows 0, 1, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 20, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34 columns gene, ensembl, Cell type): 16 is at a3 row 1 nTPM, a3 row 378 nTPM, a3 row 463 nTPM. Add those rows to the claim's evidence, or compute the number with an operation and cite that result.

limitations: A blank or missing MS intensity record represents an unmeasured gene or a level below mass spectrometry detection limits in the assay; it cannot be treated as a zero or proof of biological absence.
True median protein abundance across all 20 genes cannot be computed because 16 genes lack colon MS intensity records, and missing values cannot be substituted with numerical zeros.
Fraction of biologically absent proteins cannot be calculated from mass-spectrometry non-detection, as absence of detection does not demonstrate biological absence.
